items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 23 at 2:07PM AKST until November 23 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...High Water Levels 2 to 4 feet above the normal high
tide line.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast and Southern Seward Peninsula
Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels will coincide
with periods of high tide.
items.areas: Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 23 at 12:14PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The Department of Environmental Conservation has issued an Air
Quality Alert which is IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM AKST TUESDAY.

North Pole has a Stage 2 alert.

Fairbanks has no alert.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 23 at 12:00PM AKST until November 27 at 3:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 3 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...No additional falling snow is expected. Strong
winds will blow snow already on the ground to create areas of low
visibility near the surface. A brief decrease in winds is expected
Wednesday before winds strengthen once more Thursday.
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
items.instruction: Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 23 at 10:25AM AKST until November 24 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Ketchikan Gateway Borough.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...East to northeast winds will transition to
southeasterly with wind gusts increase through the day.
items.instruction: Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 23 at 8:00AM AKST until November 23 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Rain snow mix. Rain will freeze on contact with the ground.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted. Any rain will freeze on contact
with the ground. Surfaces may be slick.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 5:56AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Minor coastal erosion and high surf conditions are expected for
parts of the West Coast as a Bering Sea low passes by through
early Tuesday. Primarily South to Southeast wind directions could
help water levels reach 1-4 feet above the mean high tide level.
No flooding is expected.
items.areas: Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills; Yukon Delta Coast
